title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1RC1LB_1LD0RA_1LB0LE, and what is open
description: Proof status of the six-state machine 1RB1RA_1RC1LB_1LD0RA_1LB0LE_1LF1LD_---0LD: what is proved in Lean, what is computed, what is only observed.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape. This page tracks what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on. (It shares its first three states with 1RB1RA_1RC1LB_1LD0RA_---0LE_1LC0LF_1RE0LB, which has its own page; the two are different machines.)

The work has just started. The run is made of passes, and a pass is a map on the lengths of the blocks of ones; a closed form of that map is found and tested, and its pieces are proved in Lean one by one. The explainer runs the machine, its passes and the closed form in the browser.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 20,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 steps with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1011 steps.

Where it stands. At the start of each pass the tape is 1^y1 0 1^y2 0 … 0 1^yk A>0. If the closed form of the pass map holds (tested, not proved), a pass adds exactly four ones, a halt needs the last block odd and all others even (so an odd number of ones), and the only way out of the even counts is a pass whose sweep stops at a block of a single 1. So the machine halts only if the orbit of block lists ever meets such a block. In 2·107 passes it never does: after pass 50 the smallest such block is 59, and the lists have 2 to 6 blocks, all of them a fixed fraction of the tape except a tail that halves each pass.

The return map. On the closed form, every two-block state [a, 2a+d] leads in at most three passes to one with d = 1, and from [a, 2a+1] the orbit comes back to [a+12k, 2(a+12k)+1] after 9k passes. From pass 3 ([5, 11]) the orbit is a chain of such states with a = 5 mod 12, so whether the machine halts is a question about the excursion from [a, 2a+1] for almost every a. Run on residue classes of a down to mod 262, no excursion meets a stop block of 1 for 5 ≤ a < 262: if the closed form holds, no halt in the first 3.4·1018 passes.

sections.heading: The pass
paragraphs: A pass starts with A on the blank cell right of the tape. A, B and C write three ones and D turns back (start). D and E then run left writing 0 and 1 in turn (de_sweep), halving the last block into (10)^m. Where E reaches a 0 between blocks it crosses into the next block on the left (e_cross), unless that block is empty: then F reads a 0 and the machine halts. Where D reaches one, the sweep ends (d_stop), and A, B and C zigzag back to the right end, each round absorbing a 0 1 and moving a 0 one cell right (zig), until C meets a 0 at the right end and the next pass begins.

So the last block is crossed if it is odd, the blocks before it are crossed while they are even, and the sweep stops at the first odd one, yj. The closed form (py/passmap.py): if yk = 2m is even, the last block goes and the two before it each gain m+2; if yk is odd, yj-2 gains (yj−1)/2, yj-1 gains (yj+1)/2 + hj+1, and the blocks from yj on become hj+1+hj+2, …, hk-1+hk, hk−1, with hi = yi/2 and hk = (yk+5)/2. The blank on the left counts as empty blocks. A stop block yj = 1 is the one case outside the form, and there the count of ones changes by an odd number.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly in state F reading a 0, and 0 E>0 halts after one more ordinary step, whatever the rest of the tape.

claims.title: No halt in the first 20,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 20,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel. At step 17 the tape is 1^2 0 1^2 A>0, the first pass start (blank_at_17).

claims.title: The pieces of a pass, for every length
claims.text: Each phase of a pass as a theorem about any tape around it and any block length: the start, the D/E sweep over an odd or even stretch, the crossing into the next block, the end of the sweep, one round of the zigzag, and the A and B sweeps. Proved along symbolic runs (single steps by rfl, repeats by the shared crossing lemmas).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000,000 steps
claims.text: The same run for 10<sup>7</sup> steps, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The shared C simulator runs 10<sup>11</sup> steps from blank tape without a halt (15,234 ones at the end; 3,641 at 10<sup>9</sup> steps). It agrees with the Python reference simulator on the first 80 records of the run (a test).

claims.title: The closed form matches every pass of the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: Every time the head is in A on a new cell at the right end in the first 109 steps (1,005 times), the tape is blocks of ones separated by single 0s, and the block lists are exactly the orbit of the closed form from [2, 2]. Pass n starts with 4(n+1) ones. The test checks the first 108 steps.

claims.title: No simple conserved quantity
claims.text: No a·ones + b·pos + W[state] is conserved modulo 2 to 12. The count of ones is 0 mod 4 at pass starts, but not between them.

claims.title: The short chains between two-block states
claims.text: On the closed form, from [a, 2a+d]: d = 0 goes to −2, −2 to −1, 2 to −3 (one pass each), −1 to 1 and 3 to 2 (two passes), −3 to 0 (three passes), with a growing by 2, 1, 3, 2, 3, 3. So every two-block state reaches one with d = 1. Algebra from the closed form, checked on each whole residue class mod 4 by running the closed form on values p + q·u.

claims.title: The return map G(a) = a + 12k, for every a below 2<sup>62</sup>
claims.text: Run on residue classes a = p + q·u (parities known while q is even, classes split otherwise) down to a mod 262: 19,231 routes from [a, 2a+1] back to [a+12k, 2(a+12k)+1] after 9k passes, k = 1 to 10; no class halts or meets a stop block of 1; only a = 1 is set aside (it stops at a block of 1). The members below 262 of the 2,890 classes still open were run one by one and return too (k up to 11). So for every a = 1 mod 4 with 5 ≤ a < 262 the excursion is safe. 24 seconds.

claims.title: If the closed form holds: no halt in the first 3.4·10<sup>18</sup> passes
claims.text: The orbit is [5, 11] at pass 3, and the states [a, 2a+1] follow each other by G with a = 5 mod 12 (checked against the orbit for 30,000 passes). With the line above, the orbit has no halt and no stop block of 1 until a reaches 262, about pass 3.4·1018 (pass n has 3a + 1 = 4(n+1) ones). Conditional on the closed form, which is tested, not proved.

claims.title: The closed form of a pass, for every block list
claims.text: The closed form agrees with the machine on about 3,100 random block lists of up to 10 blocks of 1 to 12 ones each, every case except a stop block of 1. Not proved: the zigzag is a loop whose rounds grow, so it needs an induction in Lean on top of zig.

claims.title: The orbit stays away from a stop block of 1
claims.text: 2·107 passes of the closed form from [2, 2]: no halt, no stop block of 1 (the smallest after pass 50 is 59), 2 to 6 blocks. The two-block states are [a, 2a+d] with |d| ≤ 3, reached every 1 to 32 passes in the first 2·106; in between a tail block halves each pass (1343, 673, 338, …).

claims.title: Stop blocks stay above a fixed fraction of a
claims.text: On every route down to mod 2<sup>62</sup>, each stop block is at least about a/64; the worst fraction shrinks like 2<sup>−m/10</sup> with the depth m of the residue class (a = 2<sup>r</sup> + 1: about a·2<sup>−r/10</sup>). A stop block of 1 would need the fraction to shrink like 2<sup>−m</sup>. The route list is infinite: the tail left by the first pass lives v<sub>2</sub>(a−1) passes, so k is unbounded, and the front runs nested excursions inside it; for each k the routes are finite (k = 1 to 5 need a mod 2<sup>8</sup>, 2<sup>17</sup>, 2<sup>26</sup>, 2<sup>35</sup>, 2<sup>44</sup>).

claims.title: A proof of the pass map, and an induction for the excursion
claims.text: Prove the closed form in Lean (an induction for the zigzag, then the cases of the sweep). Then the excursion from [a, 2a+1] for every a: the route list is infinite because of the halving tail and the loops it nests, so this needs an induction on the tail length showing that stop blocks stay above a fraction of a that shrinks slower than 1/a.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
